title: Runtime plugin compatibility exemption and adapter migration policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a focused semantic versioning policy and exemption workflow for the runtime plugin/adaptor surface (third-party adapters, language-client shims, and in-process kernels). This ticket codifies: (1) what constitutes a breaking change for plugin interfaces, (2) a temporary compatibility-exemption process for urgent runtime improvements, (3) required deprecation headers and runtime telemetry, and (4) migration tooling requirements for client adapters and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Written policy doc that clearly enumerates breaking vs non-breaking changes for the plugin/adaptor API surface
A documented and gated 'compatibility exemption' request workflow with approval matrix (owner, security, release engineering)
Deprecation header spec and automatic warning emission for client adapters (HTTP header + structured logs) implemented in runtime-2.0 branch
Prototype of an 'adapter-migration-assistant' CLI that emits per-client migration hints and can run a dry-run against traffic samples
Integration tests that simulate adapter surface changes and validate rollout gates and automatic rollback on compatibility signals
tasks: Draft initial policy and example change classification matrix
Prototype header-based deprecation warning in runtime HTTP layer
Add telemetry events for 'adapter-mismatch' and 'compat-exemption-approved' to observability schema
Implement CLI skeleton for adapter-migration-assistant and a 'compat-check' mode
Define approver list and SLA for compatibility-exemption requests
Write integration tests using the adapter test harness (integration/runtime-adapter-tests)
Coordinate security review for exemption process (KMS/HSM implications where applicable)
design_decisions: Treat the plugin/adaptor surface as 'compatibility-sensitive' and require minor version bumps for behavioral changes that can break persisted client expectations
Allow a time-boxed compatibility exemption (max 7 days in prod) only with explicit rollbacks and observability hooks
Emitted deprecation headers will include 'Deprecation-Version', 'Removal-Version' and a 'Compat-Guide-URL' pointing to per-adapter migration notes
Migration tooling will not attempt automatic code transforms initially — it will provide deterministic hints and a dry-run capability to surface failures
Compatibility telemetry will be opt-in per-tenant during the initial rollout to respect privacy and regulated deployments
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Exemption process abused to introduce regressions. Mitigation: require two approvers (runtime owner + release engineer) and a mandatory canary window with explicit rollback criteria.
Risk: Third-party adapter authors ignore deprecation headers. Mitigation: Add SDK-level warnings, publish migration guides, and include adapter health signals in Console dashboards.
Risk: Telemetry leaks customer data. Mitigation: Limit telemetry to schema-approved fields and honor private deployment opt-outs; security review required.

Risk: Migration tooling produces false negatives on exotic client usage. Mitigation: Start with conservative checks, expand corpus of sampled traces for more coverage, and add per-adapter test harnesses.
